key_insight: The paper introduces an all-valid-state HOBO encoding that reuses otherwise invalid states and removes one penalty term, making VQE more reliable for constrained combinatorial optimization like TSP on NISQ devices.
engineering_relevance: This encoding can improve solution feasibility and scalability for quantum optimization workflows, especially when mapping real-world constrained problems onto current quantum hardware.
method: Construct a higher-order binary optimization (HOBO) Hamiltonian for TSP using an efficient binary representation.
Propose AVS-HOBO via cyclic mapping to eliminate one penalty term and turn invalid states into usable states.
Test noiseless simulations up to 20-city TSP instances and run experiments on real quantum devices with error mitigation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparisons between original HOBO and AVS-HOBO across energy convergence, approximation, tour-length, and feasibility ratios, plus evaluations on multiple hardware architectures and mitigation settings.
watch_item: Performance gains are shown in simulation and hardware tests, but results may still depend on device noise, architecture, and the overhead/quality of chosen error-mitigation methods.
paper_title: All-valid-state HOBO encoding for constrained combinatorial optimization on NISQ devices
